recipes.title: Phulka (soft chapati)
recipes.sub: Everyday whole-wheat flatbread, puffed over the flame
recipes.intro: A phulka is a chapati cooked without oil and puffed over an open flame, so it's soft, light and quick. Every step below affects whether it puffs, which is why the method is written out in full.

items.name: Whole-wheat atta
items.note: about 2 cups, plus 3 tbsp for dusting

items.name: Water, room temperature
items.note: warm in cool weather; hold back the last few spoons

items.name: Ghee
items.note: optional; about ¼ tsp per phulka

steps: Mix (2 min). Put the atta and salt in a wide bowl or a rimmed plate. Make a well, pour in most of the water and stir with the fingers of one hand in circles, drawing flour into the water, until it forms rough, shaggy lumps. Add the rest of the water a tablespoon at a time, only where flour is still dry. Atta brands absorb differently, so you may need a little more or less.

Knead (4 min). Gather the dough into one mass. Push it away with the heel of your hand, fold it back over itself, turn the bowl a quarter turn and repeat. Wet your fingers if it feels stiff; dust a pinch of atta if it sticks. Knead in the oil in the last minute.
Rest (15–20 min). Cover with a damp cloth or an upturned bowl. Cook your curry or dal in this time.

Divide (2 min). Knead for 20 seconds, roll into a log and cut it into equal pieces of about 30 g, the size of a golf ball (4 cm): 4 per serving. Roll each between your palms into a smooth ball with no cracks, flatten slightly and keep covered.
Set up two burners. Tawa on Burner 3 over medium-high; Burner 4 on medium for puffing, with tongs beside it. The tawa is ready when a few drops of water sizzle away in 2–3 seconds.

Roll (30 s each). Dip a ball in dry atta on both sides. Roll from the centre outward with light, even pressure, turning the disc a quarter turn every 2–3 strokes, to a 15–16 cm (6-inch) circle about 2 mm thick. Pat off loose flour; it burns on the tawa and tastes bitter.
First side (15–20 s). Lay the chapati on the tawa. Flip it as soon as small bubbles appear and the colour dulls slightly.
Second side (30–40 s). Cook until light brown spots appear underneath.

Puff (5 s). Lift it with tongs and set it on the Burner 4 flame, first side down. It balloons in 2–3 seconds; flip it for one second and take it off. No open flame? Press the edges gently with a folded cloth while it's still on the tawa.
Stack. Brush with ghee if you like and stack in a cloth-lined casserole or a box with a lid; the trapped steam keeps them soft.

tips.title: The rhythm that saves time
tips.text: Roll the next chapati while the current one is on the tawa. With practice each phulka takes about a minute: 4 in 5 minutes, 8 in 10. While you're learning, roll 3 ahead and keep them under a dry cloth.

tips.title: Without a fridge
tips.text: Use dough within about 4 hours, covered, in a cool spot; throw it away if it smells sour. Cooked phulkas, wrapped in a cloth inside a closed box, keep until the next morning; warm them 10 seconds a side on the tawa.

var: Perfect circles. Roll roughly round, press a 6-inch steel lid on top and lift away the trimmings; re-roll the scraps.
Reheat in the sandwich maker. Last night's phulkas warm through in 20–30 seconds in the closed, preheated sandwich maker, with no flipping.
Didn't puff?. The usual causes are uneven rolling, a tear, dough that's too stiff, a tawa that isn't hot enough, or too much dry flour on the surface.
cues: TOUCH Kneaded dough is soft and smooth, like an earlobe. A fingertip pressed in leaves a dent that slowly springs back. Stiff dough makes hard chapatis; sticky dough tears.
LOOK An evenly rolled phulka puffs into one balloon. Puffing only in patches means uneven thickness.
recipes.why: Resting relaxes the gluten, so the dough rolls thin without shrinking back. Even thickness matters because the steam that puffs a phulka escapes through any thin spot or tear.

recipes.title: Paratha: plain or stuffed
recipes.sub: Layered triangle, aloo or paneer · the weekend breakfast
recipes.intro: Parathas are richer than phulkas and keep you full for longer, which makes them a good weekend breakfast. The paneer version is the high-protein choice.

items.name: Water
items.note: for a slightly firmer dough than phulka

steps: Make the dough. Mix and knead as for phulka, using a little less water so the dough is soft but slightly firmer. Cover and rest 15 minutes.

Make the filling. Paneer: mix everything with your fingers. Aloo: mash the potatoes while still warm until completely smooth (lumps tear the dough), then mix in the rest. Either filling must be dry; wet filling leaks.
Divide. Make dough balls of about 80 g (2 per serving), and divide the filling into the same number of portions, each about the size of a dough ball.

Stuff and seal. Roll a dough ball to a 10 cm circle, thicker in the middle than at the edges. Put the filling in the centre, bring the edges up around it like a pouch, pinch them together at the top and twist off any extra dough. Flatten gently, seam side down.
Roll. Dust both sides with atta and roll gently from the centre outward to 15–17 cm (6–7 inches), turning often. If filling peeks through, patch it with a pinch of dry atta.

Cook (3–4 min each). Tawa on medium. Cook the first side for about a minute, until small brown spots appear, and flip. Spread ½ tsp ghee on top, flip, and spread ½ tsp on the other side. Keep cooking, pressing gently with a flat spatula and flipping every 30 seconds, until both sides are golden with crisp brown spots.
var: Plain triangle paratha. Roll a dough ball to 12 cm, brush with ¼ tsp ghee, fold in half, brush again and fold into a triangle. Roll to a 15 cm triangle and cook as above.

Air-fryer parathas. Less ghee and no standing at the tawa: preheat to 200 °C, brush each rolled paratha with ¼ tsp ghee a side and cook about 4 minutes a side, until golden with brown spots. One at a time unless two fit flat. They come out a little crisper than tawa parathas.
Methi paratha. Knead 1 cup finely chopped fresh methi leaves, ¼ tsp turmeric, ½ tsp chilli powder and ½ tsp ajwain into the dough; roll and cook like a plain paratha.

recipes.title: Ragi rotti
recipes.sub: Karnataka finger-millet flatbread · patted by hand, no rolling
recipes.intro: A Bengaluru breakfast staple. The dough is patted out with wet fingers instead of rolled, so it's quick once you have the knack. Ragi is filling and rich in fibre; pair it with something high in protein.
steps: Mix. Combine the flour, vegetables, herbs, cumin and salt. Add the warm water a little at a time and knead for a minute into a soft dough like modelling clay: it shouldn't crack at the edges when pressed, or stick to your hands.
Divide. Make 2 balls per serving.

Pat. Cut open a clean milk packet (or use butter paper) and grease it with a few drops of oil. Put a ball in the centre and pat it out with wet fingers into a 15 cm circle about 3–4 mm thick, dipping your fingers in water whenever the dough sticks. Poke 4–5 holes with a finger.

Cook. Heat the tawa on medium. Flip the sheet onto the tawa, dough side down, and peel the sheet away. Drizzle ½ tsp oil into the holes and around the edge. Cover with a lid and cook 2–3 minutes, until the edges look dry and the underside has brown spots. Flip, add ½ tsp oil and cook 1–2 minutes more, uncovered.
var: More protein. Replace 40 g of the ragi flour with besan (+3 g protein per serving), and serve with an egg.
Akki rotti. The same method with rice flour mixed with hot water instead of ragi; add grated cucumber or carrot.
cues: LOOK Cracks at the edges while you pat mean the dough is too dry: knead in 1–2 tbsp water.

recipes.title: Rice, cooked right
recipes.sub: Pressure cooker or open pot
recipes.intro: Two rices cover most meals: sona masoori is the everyday South Indian rice, and basmati is for pulao, fried rice and jeera rice. 75 g of raw rice makes about 1¼ cups cooked.

items.name: Water for sona masoori
items.note: 2 × the rice volume; 2½ × for soft rice

steps: Wash. Rinse the rice in a bowl 3 times, swirling gently, until the water is only slightly cloudy. Soak basmati 15–20 minutes; sona masoori can go straight in, or soak 10 minutes for softer rice.

Pressure cooker. Rice and water go into the cooker (or into a container on a trivet with 1 cup of water in the base). Sona masoori: 3 whistles on medium. Basmati: 1 whistle. Let the pressure drop by itself, then fluff with a fork.

Open pot (basmati). Bring the measured water to a boil with a pinch of salt and ½ tsp ghee. Add the drained rice, stir once, cover tightly and cook on the lowest flame for 12 minutes. Turn off and leave covered for 5 minutes, then fluff.
With dal. See Pot-in-pot in Part 1: dal below, rice above, 3 whistles.

tips.title: Food safety
tips.text: Eat cooked rice within 2 hours, or pack it piping hot into a preheated insulated box. Never keep cooked rice overnight without a fridge.

var: Jeera rice and lemon rice. See Book 1, Quick everyday rice.

recipes.title: Moong dal chilla
recipes.sub: Split yellow moong pancakes · soak the night before
recipes.intro: High in protein, light and quick once the dal is soaked. Use split yellow moong dal (hesaru bele), not whole green moong.
steps: Soak (the night before). Wash the dal 3 times and soak it in 2 cups of water: at least 3 hours, and overnight is fine.

Grind (2 min). Drain. Grind with the ginger, chillies, cumin and salt, adding the water a little at a time, to a smooth batter that pours like dosa batter: thick enough to coat a spoon, thin enough to spread. Stir in the hing, onion and coriander.
Heat the tawa. Medium heat. Wipe the tawa with a few drops of oil on a folded cloth or half an onion.
Spread. Pour a ladle of batter (about ⅓ cup) into the centre and spread it outward in circles with the back of the ladle to 15 cm. Drizzle ½ tsp oil around the edge.
Cook (3 min). Cook 1½–2 minutes, until the top looks dry and the edges turn golden and lift. Flip and cook 1 minute.

tips.title: Split yellow or whole green?
tips.text: Split yellow moong dal (hesaru bele) is husked and split: small, flat and yellow. Whole green moong (hesaru kaalu) still has its green skin. It makes good chillas too (that's Andhra pesarattu), but it needs a full 6–8 hours of soaking and gives a coarser, greener batter.

var: Paneer chilla. Sprinkle 50 g grated paneer and a pinch of chaat masala on each chilla after flipping, and fold (+9 g protein per chilla).
cues: LOOK If the batter tears as you spread it, it's too thick: stir in 1–2 tbsp water. Sticking means the tawa isn't hot enough or needs a little more oil.

recipes.title: Besan chilla
recipes.sub: Gram-flour pancakes · no soaking
recipes.intro: The fastest high-protein breakfast that needs no planning: besan keeps for weeks, and the batter takes three minutes.
steps: Whisk the batter (3 min). Whisk the besan with a third of the water into a thick, smooth paste with no lumps, then whisk in the rest. It should flow slowly off the spoon, like dosa batter. Stir in everything else and rest 5 minutes.
Cook. As for moong dal chilla: medium tawa, spread a ladle of batter to 15 cm, ½ tsp oil around the edge, 2 minutes until the top is dry and the edges lift, then flip for 1 minute.
var: Paneer-stuffed. When you have fresh paneer, mix 100 g grated paneer with a pinch each of salt, pepper and chaat masala. Spread a quarter on each chilla after flipping, and fold (+9 g protein per serving).
Vegetable. Add 3 tbsp grated carrot or finely chopped spinach to the batter.

recipes.title: Egg bhurji and masala omelette
recipes.sub: Indian scrambled eggs · 10 minutes
recipes.intro: Eggs keep for a week without a fridge and cook in minutes, which makes them the backbone of fast breakfasts. Bhurji also fills sandwiches and rolls.

items.name: Garam masala or pav bhaji masala

steps: Beat the eggs. Beat them with the salt until the whites and yolks are fully mixed.
Cook the masala. Heat the oil on medium. Cook the onion 3 minutes until soft, add the chilli and tomato and cook 2 minutes until soft, then the powders for 10 seconds.
Scramble. Lower the heat and pour in the eggs. Let them set for 20–30 seconds, then push slowly from the edges to the centre with a spatula for 1–2 minutes.
Stop early. Take the pan off the heat while the eggs still look slightly glossy; they keep cooking. Stir in the coriander.
var: Sandwich-maker omelette pockets. Beat 2 eggs with 1 tbsp each of finely chopped onion, tomato and coriander and a pinch each of chilli, turmeric and salt. Brush the preheated plates with oil, pour the egg into the lower plates, close gently and cook 4–5 minutes until puffed and set. If your plates leak at the hinge, use less egg.

Masala omelette. Beat the eggs with all the chopped vegetables and spices. For each omelette, heat 1 tsp oil in a pan on medium, pour in the mixture and swirl. Cook 1½ minutes until set underneath and almost set on top, flip and cook 30 seconds.

recipes.title: Kanda poha with peanuts
recipes.sub: Flattened rice with onion and peanuts · 20 minutes
recipes.intro: A light, quick breakfast from Maharashtra to Karnataka, where it's called avalakki. Peanuts add protein and crunch; add paneer on days you have it.

items.name: Thick poha (avalakki)
items.note: about 2 cups; thick or medium, not thin

steps: Rinse the poha. Put it in a colander and rinse under running water for 15–20 seconds, tossing with your fingers, until just moistened. Don't soak it; soaked poha turns to mush. Drain and leave 10 minutes to soften, then sprinkle the salt, sugar and turmeric over it and toss gently.
Fry the peanuts. Heat the oil on medium and fry the peanuts 2–3 minutes, until they crackle and darken a shade. Lift them out.
Temper. In the same oil, add the mustard seeds; when they crackle, add the curry leaves and chillies for 10 seconds, then the onion. Cook 3 minutes until soft and translucent, not brown.
Combine. Add the poha and peanuts and toss gently for 1–2 minutes. Cover and leave on the lowest flame for 2 minutes to steam.
Finish. Off the heat, squeeze over the lemon and add the coriander (and coconut).
var: Paneer poha. Add 100 g paneer in 1 cm cubes with the onion (+9 g protein per serving).
With potato. Add a small potato in 1 cm cubes before the onion; cover and cook 5 minutes until tender.
cues: TOUCH After resting, a flake should squash flat easily between your fingers. If it's still hard after cooking, sprinkle 2 tbsp water, cover and steam 1 more minute.

recipes.title: Sprout chaat
recipes.sub: Whole green moong, sprouted on your counter
recipes.intro: Sprouting needs no fridge, just a day or so on the counter. Use whole green moong (hesaru kaalu) here, not split dal.

items.name: Whole green moong
items.note: hesaru kaalu; makes about 300 g of sprouts

steps: Soak (night 1). Wash the moong and soak it in 3 cups of water for 8–10 hours.

Sprout (day 2). Drain, rinse and tip into a colander lined with a damp cotton cloth, or tie loosely in the cloth. Cover and keep in a shaded spot. Rinse and drain morning and evening. In 12–24 hours most seeds have tails 0.5–1 cm long.
Check. Sprouts should smell fresh and earthy. Throw the batch away if it smells sour or feels slimy.
Steam (4 min). Steam the sprouts for 4–5 minutes in an idli stand or a colander over boiling water, or boil 2–3 minutes and drain. Cool for a few minutes.
Toss. Mix with everything else just before eating, and eat within an hour.
recipes.why: Warm, damp sprouting conditions also suit bacteria. A short steam makes sprouts safe and easier to digest, and they keep their crunch.

recipes.title: Dal tadka
recipes.sub: Toor dal with a garlic-cumin tadka · dhaba style
recipes.intro: The everyday dal. Cooking the dal plain and adding the flavour at the end in hot ghee (the tadka) keeps it bright and aromatic.
steps: Wash and soak. Wash the dal 3 times, until the water is fairly clear. Soak 20–30 minutes if you have time.
Pressure-cook. Dal, water, turmeric and oil in the cooker. 3 whistles on medium if soaked, 4–5 if not. Let the pressure drop by itself (8–10 minutes).
Mash. Whisk the dal or mash it with a ladle until smooth and creamy. Add the salt, and hot water until it pours and flows; dal thickens as it stands.

Tadka. Heat the ghee on medium. Add the cumin; when it crackles and darkens a shade (10–15 seconds), add the garlic and cook until light golden (30 seconds), then the red chilli and hing for 5 seconds. Add the onion and cook 4–5 minutes until golden; the ginger and green chilli for 30 seconds; then the tomato with a pinch of salt for 4 minutes, until mushy with oil showing at the edges. Lower the heat and add the powders for 15 seconds.
Simmer. Pour the dal into the tadka and simmer 5 minutes on low, stirring. Crush in the kasuri methi.
Finish. Lemon juice and coriander.

tips.title: Double tadka, dhaba style
tips.text: Just before serving, heat 1 tsp ghee, fry 2 chopped garlic cloves until golden, take it off the heat, add a pinch of Kashmiri chilli powder and pour over the dal.

cues: SMELL Golden garlic smells nutty and sweet. Burnt garlic is bitter, and will make the whole dal bitter: start the tadka again.

recipes.title: Moong dal
recipes.sub: Split yellow moong dal · light and quick, no soaking
recipes.intro: The lightest, quickest dal, and the highest in protein. It pairs with anything, including a dry chicken or paneer dish for a grain-free dinner.
steps: Cook. Wash the dal 3 times. Pressure-cook with the water and turmeric, 2 whistles on medium, and let the pressure drop. (Or simmer in an open pot, partly covered, for 20 minutes, skimming off the froth.)
Whisk. Whisk until smooth, add the salt and loosen with hot water.
Tadka. Heat the ghee on medium. Cumin until it crackles; garlic until light golden; ginger, green chilli and hing for 20 seconds; tomato for 3 minutes until soft; chilli powder for 10 seconds.
Simmer. Add the dal and simmer 3 minutes. Finish with lemon and coriander.
var: Dal palak. Add the chopped spinach with the tomato and cook 2 minutes before adding the dal.

recipes.title: Sambar
recipes.sub: Karnataka-style lentil and vegetable stew with tamarind
recipes.intro: Karnataka sambar is gently sweet from a little jaggery, tangy from tamarind, and full of vegetables. Eat it with rice, or with idli and dosa on weekends.

items.name: Mixed vegetables
items.note: drumstick in 3-inch pieces, carrot, pumpkin, beans, brinjal, 6 small onions

items.name: Tamarind
items.note: a small lemon-sized ball, soaked in ½ cup hot water

steps: Cook the dal. Wash the dal and pressure-cook it with the water, turmeric and oil, 4 whistles. Mash it smooth.
Tamarind. Meanwhile, squeeze the soaked tamarind with your fingers and strain out the fibres and seeds.

Cook the vegetables. In a pot, boil the vegetables with 1½ cups of water, the salt and a pinch of turmeric, covered, 8–10 minutes, until a knife slides into the drumstick and pumpkin with slight resistance. Add brinjal for the last 5 minutes only.
Add the masala. Add the tamarind water, sambar powder and jaggery. Boil 5 minutes, until the raw tamarind smell has gone.
Add the dal. Stir in the mashed dal and add water until the sambar pours easily. Simmer 5 minutes. Taste: tangy, mildly sweet and well salted.

Temper. Heat the oil. Add the mustard; when it crackles, add the methi and let it turn light brown (dark methi is bitter), then the red chilli, curry leaves and hing. Pour over the sambar and add the coriander.

tips.title: Save a burner
tips.text: Cook the vegetables in a second container stacked over the dal in the cooker (pot-in-pot), with a little water and salt. They come out softer, which is fine in sambar.

var: Air-fryer vegetables. Toss the vegetables with ½ tsp oil and a pinch of salt and air-fry at 200 °C for 10–12 minutes, shaking twice, until browned at the edges and nearly tender. Add them with the tamarind water and simmer 6–8 minutes so they soak up the masala. It frees a burner and adds a light roasted flavour.

recipes.title: Bisi bele bath
recipes.sub: Karnataka spiced dal-rice one-pot · the lunch-box hero
recipes.intro: "Hot lentil rice": dal, rice and vegetables cooked soft in the cooker, then simmered with tamarind and bisi bele bath powder and finished with a ghee tempering. One pot, a complete meal, and it travels well in an insulated box.

items.name: Mixed vegetables, 1.5 cm pieces
items.note: carrot, beans, potato, peas, capsicum, small onions

items.name: Water
items.note: about 4½ × the dal and rice by volume

items.name: Tamarind
items.note: a small lemon-sized ball, soaked in ½ cup hot water

steps: Pressure-cook. Wash the dal and rice together 3 times. Put them in the cooker with the vegetables, water, turmeric and oil. 4 whistles on medium; let the pressure drop by itself.
Masala. Meanwhile, squeeze and strain the tamarind. Boil the tamarind water with the bisi bele bath powder, jaggery and salt for 3–4 minutes, until the raw smell has gone.

Combine. Open the cooker and mash lightly with a ladle; it should be soft and porridge-like. Stir in the masala, then add hot water until it flows softly off the spoon. It thickens a lot as it cools, especially in a lunch box. Simmer 3–4 minutes on low, stirring so it doesn't stick.
Temper. Heat the ghee, add the mustard; when it crackles, fry the cashews until golden, then the curry leaves, red chilli and hing for a few seconds. Pour over the pot.
var: Masala khichdi. Use split yellow moong dal instead of toor, and skip the tamarind and bisi bele bath powder. In the cooker base, temper 1 tbsp ghee with cumin, ginger, green chilli, onion, tomato, turmeric and ½ tsp garam masala; add the washed dal, rice, vegetables and water and cook 3 whistles.
recipes.note: For 4 servings, use a 5 L cooker.

recipes.title: Rajma masala
recipes.sub: Punjabi kidney-bean curry · soak 8 hours
recipes.intro: Creamy, rich rajma-chawal is a weekend favourite. The beans must be soaked and cooked completely soft.
steps: Soak. The night before (or that morning, for dinner), wash the rajma and soak it in 3 cups of water for 8–10 hours. They double in size.

Pressure-cook. Drain, rinse, and cook with the fresh water and salt: bring to the first whistle on high, then cook 20 minutes on the lowest flame (or 7–8 whistles on medium). Let the pressure drop. Check that a bean mashes completely; if not, cook 2–3 more whistles. Keep the cooking water.

Masala. Meanwhile, heat the oil on medium. Add the bay leaf and cumin, then the onion, and cook 8–10 minutes until deep golden; deep golden onion makes a rich rajma. Add the ginger-garlic paste and chilli for a minute, then the tomato purée, powders (except garam masala) and salt. Cook 8–10 minutes, stirring, until thick and darker, with oil separating at the edges.
Simmer. Add the rajma and its cooking water. Mash a few beans against the side of the pot to thicken the gravy and simmer 10 minutes on low; longer makes it creamier.
Finish. Garam masala, crushed kasuri methi and coriander. It should be thick but still flowing.

tips.title: Never eat undercooked rajma
tips.text: Raw or partly cooked kidney beans contain a natural toxin that causes severe stomach upset; thorough boiling destroys it. Soak the beans, throw away the soaking water, and pressure-cook until a bean mashes completely between two fingers.

recipes.title: Chole
recipes.sub: Punjabi chickpea curry · soak 8 hours
recipes.intro: Tangy, spicy chickpeas. A tea bag in the cooker gives the dark colour of restaurant chole.

items.name: Chole masala
items.note: or 1 tsp coriander powder + ½ tsp each garam masala, chilli and amchur

steps: Soak. Wash and soak the chana 8–10 hours. For a Friday dinner, soak them on Friday morning before you leave.

Pressure-cook. Drain and cook with the fresh water, tea bag and salt: first whistle on high, then 15 minutes on the lowest flame (or 6 whistles on medium). Let the pressure drop. A chickpea should crush easily between your fingers. Discard the tea bag; keep the water.

Masala. Heat the oil, add the cumin and bay leaf, then the onion for 8–10 minutes until deep golden. Add the ginger-garlic paste and chilli for a minute, then the tomato purée, chole masala, turmeric and salt. Cook 8–10 minutes until thick, with oil at the edges.
Simmer. Add the chana with enough cooking water for a thick gravy. Mash a few against the pot and simmer 10–15 minutes on low.
Finish. Amchur, ginger strips, lemon and coriander.
var: Crunchy air-fried chana. Keep back a cup of the pressure-cooked chana before the masala. Pat dry, toss with 1 tsp oil, ½ tsp chaat masala, ¼ tsp chilli powder and a pinch of salt, and air-fry at 190 °C for 15–18 minutes, shaking every 5, until crunchy. A high-protein snack; eat it the same day.

recipes.title: Palya
recipes.sub: Karnataka dry vegetable with coconut · beans, cabbage, carrot or beetroot
recipes.intro: The everyday Karnataka side: one vegetable, a quick tempering, a lid to steam it, and fresh coconut at the end. Learn it once and it works for almost any vegetable.

items.name: Vegetable, cut
items.note: beans in 5 mm rounds, cabbage shredded 2–3 mm, or carrot or beetroot in 5 mm dice

items.name: Dried red chilli or green chilli

steps: Temper. Heat the oil on medium. Add the mustard; when it crackles, add the urad and chana dal and stir 20–30 seconds until golden. Add the curry leaves, chilli and hing, then the onion (if using) for 2 minutes.
Add the vegetable. Add it with the turmeric and salt and toss for a minute to coat.
Steam. Sprinkle 2 tbsp water, cover and cook on low-medium until tender but still bright with a slight bite: cabbage 5–6 minutes, beans and carrot 7–9, beetroot 10. Stir once or twice.
Finish. Uncover and cook off any water for a minute. Off the heat, toss in the coconut, and the lemon if you like.
cues: LOOK Beans should stay bright green. Dull olive green means overcooked.

recipes.title: Aloo gobi
recipes.sub: Dry potato and cauliflower · stovetop or air fryer
recipes.intro: A dry North Indian classic for phulkas. The air-fryer method uses less oil and browns the edges nicely.
steps: Clean the cauliflower. Soak the florets in hot salted water for 10 minutes to draw out any insects, then drain well.

Cook covered. Heat the oil on medium. When the cumin crackles, add the potato, cauliflower, turmeric and salt and toss 2 minutes. Cover and cook on low-medium for 12–15 minutes, stirring gently every 3–4 minutes. Add no water; the lid traps the steam. It's ready when a knife slides into the potato.
Add the masala. Uncover, add the ginger, chilli, tomato, chilli powder and coriander powder, and cook 3–4 minutes uncovered until the tomato coats everything and the edges brown.
Finish. Garam masala, amchur and coriander.
var: Air fryer. Toss the florets and potato with 2 tsp oil, the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt. Air-fry at 200 °C for 15–18 minutes, shaking every 5, until tender with brown edges. Meanwhile, in a pan with 1 tsp oil, cook the cumin, ginger, chilli and tomato for 3 minutes; toss in the vegetables with the amchur, garam masala and coriander.

recipes.title: Bhindi masala
recipes.sub: Okra with onion masala · crisp, not slimy
recipes.intro: Okra turns slimy when it meets water or a lid. Dry it completely, cook it open over high heat (or in the air fryer), and add salt only at the end.

items.name: Bhindi (okra)
items.note: washed and dried completely before cutting

items.name: Oil
items.note: 1 tsp is enough in the air fryer

steps: Dry, then cut. Wash the bhindi, spread it on a cloth and pat dry, then leave 10 minutes to air-dry. Cut off the tops and tips and cut into 1.5–2 cm rounds.
Air fryer. Toss with 1 tsp oil, the turmeric and chilli powder. 190 °C for 10–12 minutes, shaking every 4, until the edges brown.

Or stovetop. Heat 2 tsp oil in a wide pan on medium-high. Add the bhindi in one layer with the turmeric and chilli powder and cook uncovered for 8–10 minutes, stirring every minute or two, until the edges brown and the sticky strands disappear. Never cover it.
Masala. In a pan with 1 tsp oil, crackle the cumin, cook the onion 4 minutes, the ginger-garlic paste 30 seconds and the tomato 3 minutes, then add the coriander powder.
Combine. Add the bhindi, salt, amchur and garam masala and toss 2 minutes.

recipes.title: Mushroom pepper fry
recipes.sub: Chettinad-style dry mushrooms with black pepper and curry leaves
recipes.intro: Peppery, dry and quick. Searing the mushrooms first drives off their water, so they brown instead of stewing.

items.name: Black pepper, freshly crushed
items.note: crush in a mortar; ground pepper is flatter

steps: Sear the mushrooms. Heat 1 tsp of the oil on high and cook the mushrooms 5–6 minutes, until their water evaporates and the edges brown (or air-fry at 200 °C for 8 minutes). Set aside.
Masala. Add the rest of the oil on medium. Fennel and curry leaves for 10 seconds; onion for 5 minutes until golden; ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute; then the chilli, turmeric and coriander powder.
Combine. Add the mushrooms and salt and toss 2 minutes. Add the pepper and cook 1 more minute. Finish with lemon and coriander.
var: Paneer pepper fry. Use 200 g paneer cubes instead of mushrooms; skip the searing and toss them in for only 2 minutes (about 18 g protein per serving).

recipes.title: Palak paneer
recipes.sub: Paneer in a bright spinach gravy
recipes.intro: The trick is to cook the spinach as little as possible: a 2-minute blanch, a cold rinse, and only a few minutes in the masala. That keeps it green.
steps: Blanch. Bring 1 litre of water to a boil in a wide pan. Add the spinach and chillies for 2 minutes, just until wilted and bright green. Drain and plunge into a bowl of cold tap water for a minute.
Purée. Grind the spinach and chillies with 2–3 tbsp water until smooth.
Soften the paneer. Soak the paneer cubes in warm salted water while you cook.

Masala. Heat the oil and ghee on medium. Crackle the cumin, cook the onion 5 minutes until golden, the ginger-garlic paste 1 minute, then the tomato with the salt for 3–4 minutes until mushy. Add the powders for 15 seconds.
Simmer. Add the spinach purée and ¼ cup water and simmer 3–4 minutes on low. Longer turns it olive-dark.
Finish. Add the drained paneer, crushed kasuri methi and garam masala and simmer 2 minutes. Swirl in the cream off the heat.
var: Air-fried paneer. For firmer, lightly charred paneer, toss the cubes with ½ tsp oil and air-fry at 200 °C for 6 minutes before adding them.
cues: LOOK The gravy stays bright green. Grey-olive means the spinach has cooked too long.

recipes.title: Paneer butter masala
recipes.sub: Restaurant-style creamy tomato gravy, with a lighter version
recipes.intro: Silky, mildly sweet and deep orange. The same makhani gravy is the base of butter chicken.
steps: Cook the base. Simmer the tomatoes, onion, cashews, ginger, garlic and cardamom with the water, covered, for 10 minutes until soft (or 1 whistle in the cooker). Cool 5 minutes.
Blend. Blend completely smooth. With hot liquid, fill the jar only halfway and hold the lid down with a cloth. For restaurant silkiness, push it through a strainer.

Cook the gravy. Heat the butter and oil on medium. Add the bay leaf and chilli powder for 10 seconds (don't let it burn), then the purée. Cook 8–10 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy with butter separating at the edges; this is where the flavour develops. Add the salt and sugar.
Add the paneer. Loosen with ¼–½ cup water to a flowing gravy, add the drained paneer and simmer 3–4 minutes.
Finish. Crushed kasuri methi and garam masala; stir in the cream off the heat.
var: Paneer tikka masala. Use air-fryer paneer tikka (Air fryer chapter) instead of plain cubes, and simmer only 2 minutes.
Lighter version. Use half the butter, replace the cream with milk, and add 5 more cashews to the base for creaminess.

recipes.title: Paneer bhurji
recipes.sub: Scrambled paneer · for phulkas, sandwiches and rolls
recipes.intro: The quickest paneer dish there is, and one of the highest in protein. Don't overcook it: paneer dries out fast.

items.name: Garam masala or pav bhaji masala

steps: Crumble. Crumble the paneer with your fingers into small, uneven bits, not a paste.

Masala. Heat the oil on medium. Crackle the cumin, cook the onion 3 minutes, the ginger, chilli and capsicum 1 minute, then the tomato with the salt for 3 minutes until soft. Add the powders for 15 seconds.
Paneer. Add the paneer and milk and toss 2–3 minutes on low. Finish with kasuri methi and coriander.
var: Egg and paneer bhurji. Stir in 2 beaten eggs before the paneer and scramble 1 minute (+6 g protein per serving).

recipes.title: Egg curry
recipes.sub: Boiled eggs in onion-tomato gravy · Andhra home style
recipes.intro: Boil the eggs in the air fryer while you make the gravy, and dinner is ready in half an hour.
steps: Prepare the eggs. Make 3–4 shallow slashes on each peeled egg so the gravy gets in. For a blistered finish, rub them with ¼ tsp oil and a pinch each of chilli and turmeric, and air-fry at 200 °C for 4–5 minutes.
Brown the onions. Heat the oil on medium. Cumin and curry leaves for 10 seconds, then the onion for 8 minutes until golden-brown.
Masala. Add the ginger-garlic paste and chilli for a minute, then the tomatoes and salt for 5 minutes, until mushy with oil separating. Add the powders with a splash of water and cook 30 seconds.
Gravy. Add the water and simmer 5 minutes to a medium-thick gravy.
Eggs. Add the eggs, spoon the gravy over them and simmer 3–4 minutes. Add the garam masala, and the coconut milk for the last minute (don't boil it hard). Finish with coriander.

recipes.title: Air-fryer boiled eggs
recipes.sub: No pot, no water, no watching
recipes.intro: The air fryer cooks eggs in their shells with dry heat. Load it first thing in a session and forget it until the timer goes.
steps: Load. Put the eggs in the basket in one layer, not touching. No preheating and no water.
Cook. 130 °C: 15 minutes for firm yolks, 12–13 minutes for jammy ones.
Cool. Move them straight into a bowl of cold water for 5 minutes. This stops the cooking and makes them easier to peel.
Peel. Tap all over, then peel under running water, starting from the wide end.

tips.title: Test your machine
tips.text: Air fryers vary. The first time, cook one egg and cut it open, and note the time that suits your machine. A few brown speckles on the shell are normal.

recipes.note: Keep them in their shells until you eat them, and eat them the same day (by lunchtime if packed).

recipes.title: Soya pulao
recipes.sub: One-pot rice with soya chunks and vegetables · lunch-box hero
recipes.intro: Soya chunks keep for months and have more protein by weight than chicken. Boiled, squeezed and cooked in a spiced pulao, they soak up flavour like meat.
steps: Prepare the soya. Boil the soya chunks in plenty of water with a pinch of salt for 5 minutes. Drain, rinse in cold water and squeeze each handful as hard as you can, like wringing a cloth. Halve any big ones.

Pulao base. In the cooker base, heat the oil and ghee on medium. Add the whole spices for 20 seconds, then the onion for 4–5 minutes until golden. Add the ginger-garlic paste and chillies for a minute, then the vegetables, soya, mint, powders, curd and salt, and stir 2 minutes.
Rice. Add the drained rice and stir gently for a minute. Pour in the water and lemon juice and taste the water: it should be pleasantly salty.
Cook. Close and cook 1 whistle on medium. Let the pressure drop for 5–8 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
var: Meatier soya. After squeezing, toss the soya with the curd, chilli powder and a pinch of salt and air-fry at 200 °C for 6–8 minutes, shaking once, before adding it to the pulao base.
Sona masoori instead of basmati. Use twice the rice volume of water and 2 whistles.
recipes.why: Squeezed soya soaks up the masala like a sponge. Chunks left wet stay bland and spongy.

recipes.title: Egg fried rice
recipes.sub: Indo-Chinese street style · eggs, vegetables, soy and pepper
recipes.intro: The rice must be cooked firm and cooled until dry, so it fries instead of steaming. Keep the heat as high as it goes and keep everything moving.

items.name: Salt
items.note: taste first; soy sauce is salty

steps: Cook and cool the rice. Pressure-cook the rice firm, then spread it on a wide plate under the fan for 10 minutes. Hot, wet rice turns mushy in the wok.
Scramble the eggs. Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper. Heat 1 tsp of the oil in a wok or kadai on high and scramble them into soft curds, about a minute. Take them out.
Aromatics. Add the rest of the oil on high. Garlic, ginger, chilli and spring-onion whites for 30 seconds.
Vegetables. Add the vegetables and toss 2–3 minutes; they should stay crisp.
Rice. Add the rice and break up any clumps. Add the soy sauce, vinegar, pepper and salt and toss 2 minutes on high, so the rice heats evenly and toasts a little.
Finish. Return the eggs, toss, and add the spring-onion greens.

recipes.title: Home-style chicken curry
recipes.sub: Bone-in chicken in onion-tomato masala · pressure-cooker option
recipes.intro: The colour and sweetness of a good chicken curry come from onions cooked slowly to deep golden. Give them the full 12 minutes.
steps: Marinate. Mix the chicken with the marinade and leave it while you chop (20 minutes is plenty; never more than 2 hours without a fridge).
Onions. Heat the oil on medium. Add the whole spices for 20 seconds, then the onions. Cook 10–12 minutes, stirring every minute, until deep golden-brown; add a splash of water if they stick.
Ginger-garlic. Add the paste and chillies and cook 1 minute, until the raw smell has gone.
Tomatoes. Add the tomatoes and salt and cook 5–6 minutes until mushy, with oil showing at the edges. Add the powders with 2 tbsp water and cook 30 seconds.
Bhuna. Add the chicken with its marinade and cook on high for 5–6 minutes, stirring, until the chicken is white outside and coated in masala.
Simmer. Add the hot water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 15–18 minutes. (Or close the cooker: 2 whistles on medium, then let the pressure drop.)
Finish. Garam masala and coriander. Adjust the gravy with water or by simmering uncovered, and rest 5 minutes.
var: Air-fryer start. Air-fry the marinated chicken at 200 °C for 10 minutes, turning once, while the onions cook. Skip the bhuna in step 5: add the chicken to the finished masala with the water and simmer 10–12 minutes. Less stirring and a deeper, roasted flavour.
cues: LOOK Done when the meat at the bone shows no pink and the juices run clear.

recipes.title: Butter chicken
recipes.sub: Air-fried tikka in makhani gravy
recipes.intro: Restaurant butter chicken is tandoor-charred tikka simmered in a smooth tomato-butter gravy. The air fryer does the charring.
steps: Marinate. Mix the chicken with the tikka ingredients and leave 30 minutes to 2 hours.
Gravy base. Meanwhile, simmer the tomatoes, cashews, ginger and garlic with the water, covered, for 10 minutes. Cool, then blend completely smooth (fill the jar only halfway).
Tikka. Air-fry the chicken at 200 °C for 12–14 minutes, turning halfway, until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Cook the gravy. Heat the butter on medium, add the chilli powder for 10 seconds, then the purée. Cook 8–10 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy. Add the salt and sugar.
Combine. Add the tikka and enough water for a flowing gravy and simmer 5 minutes. Add the kasuri methi and garam masala, and stir in the cream off the heat.
var: No air fryer. Sear the chicken in a hot pan with 2 tsp oil for 6–8 minutes, turning, until charred and cooked through.
cues: LOOK Cut the biggest tikka before it goes into the gravy: no pink inside.

recipes.title: Air-fryer tandoori chicken
recipes.sub: The highest-protein dinner in the book, with almost no oil
recipes.intro: Breast chunks in a hung-curd marinade, air-fried until charred. With moong dal and a salad it's a light, high-protein dinner with no grain needed.

items.name: Hung curd
items.note: thick curd squeezed in a cloth for 15 minutes

items.name: Onion rings, lemon wedges, chaat masala, green chutney

steps: Marinate. Pat the chicken dry. Mix in everything except half the oil and leave 30 minutes to 2 hours.
Preheat. Air fryer at 200 °C for 3 minutes.
Cook. Lay the chicken in one layer, brush with the remaining oil and cook 12–14 minutes, turning halfway (bone-in leg pieces, slashed: 18–20 minutes).
Rest. Rest 3 minutes, then finish with chaat masala and lemon.

tips.title: Juicy breast
tips.text: Breast dries out when overcooked. Check a piece at 12 minutes: no pink inside means it's done.

var: Fish tikka. Use firm fish (seer) in 4 cm chunks; marinate only 20 minutes and cook 8–10 minutes.

recipes.title: Pepper chicken fry
recipes.sub: Dry boneless chicken with black pepper · high protein, ready in 35 minutes
recipes.intro: A South Indian dry chicken that goes with phulkas, rice and dal, or on its own with salad. Boneless thigh stays juiciest.
steps: Marinate. Mix the chicken with the marinade and leave 15 minutes while you chop.
Masala. Heat the oil on medium. Fennel and curry leaves for 10 seconds, then the onion for 6–7 minutes until golden, and the chillies.
Sear. Add the chicken on high heat and stir 5 minutes, until it turns white all over. Add the coriander powder and half the pepper.
Cook covered. Cover and cook on medium-low for 8–10 minutes (breast: 6–7), stirring twice.
Dry it out. Uncover, turn the heat to high and stir 3–4 minutes until the masala clings and the pan is almost dry. Add the rest of the pepper, the garam masala, lemon and coriander.
var: Air-fryer route. Air-fry the marinated chicken at 200 °C for 10–12 minutes, turning once, while you make the onion masala. Toss it into the masala with the coriander powder and pepper and stir on high for 3 minutes. No covered cooking, and far less stirring.
cues: LOOK Cut the biggest piece: no pink inside and the juices clear.

recipes.title: Coastal fish curry
recipes.sub: Karnataka coast style · tamarind and coconut milk
recipes.intro: Tangy with tamarind and mellowed with coconut milk. Mackerel (bangude) is cheap and very Mangalorean; seer (anjal) and pomfret are milder.

items.name: Fish steaks
items.note: seer, pomfret or mackerel, cleaned as in Book 1

items.name: Thick coconut milk
items.note: tetra packs keep unopened without a fridge

steps: Marinate. Rub the fish with the turmeric, salt and lemon and leave 10 minutes.
Temper. Heat the oil on medium. Add the mustard; when it crackles, the methi until light brown, then the curry leaves.

Masala. Cook the onion 5 minutes until soft and golden, the ginger-garlic paste 1 minute, the chillies, then the tomato for 3 minutes. Lower the heat and add the powders with 2 tbsp water for a minute; chilli burns easily.
Gravy. Add the tamarind, water and salt and boil 4–5 minutes to a thin gravy.
Fish. Slide in the fish in one layer. Cover and simmer on low for 5–7 minutes. Don't stir: swirl the pan and spoon gravy over the fish.

Coconut milk. When the fish is opaque and flakes at the thickest part, pour in the coconut milk and heat 2 minutes without letting it boil hard; coconut milk splits if boiled fast. Rest 10 minutes before serving; the flavour deepens.
var: Firmer fish. Air-fry the marinated fish at 200 °C for 5 minutes before sliding it into the gravy, then simmer only 3–4 minutes. The pieces hold together better, which helps with soft fish like pomfret.
Fish rava fry. The dry, crisp version is in the Air fryer chapter.

recipes.title: Mutton curry
recipes.sub: Pressure-cooker mutton in onion-tomato gravy
recipes.intro: A weekend curry. Choose young goat from the shoulder and leg (see Book 1's Prep school) and let the pressure cooker make it tender.
steps: Marinate. Mix the mutton with the marinade and leave 30 minutes to 1½ hours (no longer without a fridge).
Onions. In the cooker base, heat the oil and ghee on medium. Whole spices for 20 seconds, then the onions for 10–12 minutes until deep golden.
Masala. Add the tomatoes, chillies and powders (not the garam masala) and cook 5 minutes until the oil separates.
Bhuna. Add the mutton with its marinade and cook on high for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until the surface browns and the masala clings.
Pressure-cook. Add the hot water, close, and cook 5–6 whistles on medium (young goat 4–5), then 5 minutes on the lowest flame. Let the pressure drop by itself (10–15 minutes).

Check and finish. A knife should slide in with slight resistance and the meat should come off the bone easily; if not, 1–2 more whistles. Simmer uncovered to the thickness you like, then add the garam masala, coriander and mint.

recipes.title: Egg-paneer kathi rolls
recipes.sub: Phulka rolls for the lunch box · Kolkata street style
recipes.intro: A dry filling rolled in an egg-coated phulka travels well at room temperature until lunch, and two rolls carry more than 30 g of protein.

items.name: Oil
items.note: ½ tsp per roll, plus 2 tsp for the filling

items.name: Onion, thinly sliced, with lemon and chaat masala

steps: Filling. Heat 2 tsp oil on high. Cook the onion and capsicum 2 minutes, then the paneer, sauce, chaat masala and salt for 2 minutes.

Egg layer. Beat one egg with a pinch of salt. Heat ½ tsp oil on the tawa over medium, pour in the egg and spread it to the size of the phulka. Immediately press a phulka on top. Cook 1 minute until the egg sets, flip and cook 20 seconds.
Roll. Egg side up: spread chutney, add a quarter of the filling and the onions, and roll tightly. Wrap the bottom half in butter paper or foil.
Pack. Let the rolls cool 5 minutes before wrapping, so steam doesn't make them soggy. Eat by lunchtime.
var: Chicken or tikka roll. Use air-fryer tandoori chicken strips or paneer tikka instead of the paneer filling.
Toasted roll. If your sandwich maker has flat or ribbed grill plates, press the finished roll in it for 2 minutes for a crisp outside that holds together in the lunch box.

recipes.title: Air-fryer paneer tikka
recipes.sub: Charred, smoky paneer with capsicum and onion
recipes.intro: Restaurant paneer tikka without a tandoor. Hung curd makes the marinade cling and adds protein; roasted besan helps it stick.

items.name: Onion, quartered and separated into petals

steps: Roast the besan. Stir it in a dry pan on low for 1–2 minutes until it smells nutty; raw besan tastes pasty.
Marinate. Whisk the hung curd with everything except the paneer and vegetables. Fold in the paneer, capsicum and onion gently and leave 20 minutes (up to an hour).
Arrange. Preheat to 200 °C for 3 minutes. Lay the pieces in one layer, not touching, or thread them on wooden skewers soaked in water for 20 minutes.
Air-fry. 8–10 minutes, turning once at 5, until the edges are charred in spots. Don't go longer: paneer turns chewy.
Finish. Sprinkle with chaat masala and squeeze over some lemon.
var: Paneer tikka masala. Simmer the tikka for 2 minutes in the makhani gravy from the paneer butter masala card.
Roll or sandwich. Roll in a phulka with green chutney and onions, or fill a sandwich-maker sandwich.

recipes.title: Air-fryer chicken seekh kebab
recipes.sub: Spiced chicken-mince kebabs · ask the shop to mince it fresh
recipes.intro: Ask the chicken shop to mince boneless thigh, or half thigh and half breast, while you wait. Squeezing the water out of the onion and herbs, and kneading the mince well, keeps the kebabs from falling apart.

items.name: Onion, very finely chopped
items.note: small; squeezed dry in a cloth

items.name: Oil or melted butter, for brushing

steps: Roast the besan. Stir it in a dry pan on low for 1–2 minutes until nutty.
Knead. Put everything except the oil in a bowl and knead with your hand for 2 minutes, until the mixture turns sticky and holds together. This binds the mince so the kebabs don't crack.
Shape. With wet hands, divide into 3 portions per serving and roll each into a log about 10 cm long and 2.5 cm thick (or press it around a soaked wooden skewer). Smooth out any cracks.
Air-fry. Preheat to 200 °C. Brush the kebabs with oil, lay them in one layer and cook 12–14 minutes, turning at 7, until browned with charred spots.
Check. Cut the thickest one: no pink inside, and the juices run clear. Rest 2 minutes.
recipes.note: Buy the mince on the day and cook it within 2 hours: minced meat spoils faster than whole pieces.

recipes.title: Air-fryer fish rava fry
recipes.sub: Mangalorean semolina-crusted fish · crisp with 2 tsp of oil
recipes.intro: In Mangalore, masala-rubbed fish is pressed into rava and shallow-fried. The air fryer gives the same crunch with a fraction of the oil. Seer (anjal), pomfret and mackerel (bangude) all work.
steps: Marinate (10–15 min). Pat the fish dry. Mix the masala into a thick paste with no water, rub it all over the fish and leave 10–15 minutes, no longer.
Coat. Mix the rava, rice flour, chilli and salt on a plate. Press each piece into it firmly on both sides so the coating sticks.
Air-fry. Preheat to 200 °C. Brush the fish with oil on both sides, lay it in one layer and cook 10–12 minutes, turning carefully with a flat spatula at 6.
cues: LOOK The crust is golden and crisp, and the flesh at the thickest part is opaque and flakes easily.

recipes.title: Air-fryer hara bhara kabab
recipes.sub: Spinach, peas, potato and paneer patties
recipes.intro: A green vegetarian kabab with paneer for protein. Blanched spinach and peas are pulsed coarse, bound with potato and roasted besan, and air-fried crisp.

items.name: Green peas
items.note: fresh, or dried peas soaked and boiled soft

steps: Blanch. Boil the spinach for 1 minute and fresh peas for 3–4 minutes in salted water; drain and cool in cold water. Squeeze the spinach completely dry; wet spinach makes soft kababs that fall apart.
Pulse. Pulse the spinach, peas, chillies, ginger and coriander in the mixie 4–5 times, to a coarse mixture rather than a paste.
Mix. Combine with the potato, paneer, roasted besan, spices, salt and lemon. Pressed in your hand it should hold together; add 1 tbsp more besan if it's sticky.
Shape. Make 3 patties per serving, about 6 cm across and 1.5 cm thick, with smooth edges.
Air-fry. Preheat to 200 °C. Brush the kababs with oil on both sides and cook 12–14 minutes, turning at 7, until crisp outside.

recipes.title: Air-fryer soya cutlets
recipes.sub: Crisp high-protein patties · snack, breakfast or sandwich filling
recipes.intro: Soya, potato and vegetables shaped into patties and air-fried crisp with two teaspoons of oil instead of a pan of it.
steps: Prepare the soya. Boil the chunks 5 minutes, drain, rinse in cold water and squeeze them very dry. Pulse in the mixie 5–6 times to a coarse mince.
Mix. Combine everything except the oil. Pressed in your hand, the mixture should hold together; if it's sticky, add 1 tbsp more besan.
Shape. Divide into 3 per serving and shape into patties about 7 cm across and 1.5 cm thick, smoothing the edges; cracked edges break in the fryer.
Air-fry. Preheat to 200 °C. Brush the cutlets with oil on both sides, lay them in one layer and cook 12–14 minutes, turning at 7, until golden and crisp.

recipes.title: Masala peanuts, roasted chana and makhana
recipes.sub: Crunchy high-protein snacks from the air fryer
recipes.intro: Make a batch on Sunday and keep it in airtight jars for the week. A handful replaces biscuits or chips as the afternoon snack.
steps: Coat the peanuts. Toss the peanuts with the oil and water so they're just damp. Sprinkle over the besan, rice flour, spices and salt and toss until every peanut has a dry, sandy coat.
Air-fry. 160 °C for 12–15 minutes, shaking every 4 minutes, until the coating is crisp and the peanuts crackle. They crisp more as they cool.
Chana. Toss the roasted chana with the oil, chaat masala and chilli. Air-fry with the curry leaves at 160 °C for 4–5 minutes.
Makhana. Toss the makhana with the ghee, chaat masala, pepper and salt. Air-fry at 150 °C for 8–10 minutes, shaking twice, until one crunches right through when you bite it.
Store. Cool completely before putting them in airtight jars; warm snacks sweat and go soft.
var: Plain roasted peanuts. 160 °C for 10 minutes, shaking twice. Rub off the skins if you like.

recipes.title: Egg-bhurji sandwich
recipes.sub: Sandwich-maker meals
recipes.intro: One serving of egg bhurji (3 eggs) fills 2 sandwiches: about 28 g of protein for the pair.
recipes.parentIntro: The sandwich maker toasts and seals in 3–4 minutes with no flipping. The method is the same for every filling: preheat until the ready light comes on, butter the outsides thinly (¼ tsp a side), don't overfill, toast 3–4 minutes until golden, and let it rest a minute before biting; the filling is very hot.

items.name: Half a serving of egg bhurji (1½ eggs)

steps: Spread the chutney on the inside of the bread, add the bhurji, close and butter the outsides. Toast 3–4 minutes and cut along the seal.

recipes.title: Paneer bhurji sandwich
recipes.sub: Sandwich-maker meals
recipes.intro: About 14 g of protein per sandwich.
recipes.parentIntro: The sandwich maker toasts and seals in 3–4 minutes with no flipping. The method is the same for every filling: preheat until the ready light comes on, butter the outsides thinly (¼ tsp a side), don't overfill, toast 3–4 minutes until golden, and let it rest a minute before biting; the filling is very hot.

items.name: Half a serving of paneer bhurji (50 g paneer)

steps: As above. Made with fresh paneer, so cook it the same morning you buy it.

recipes.title: Paneer tikka sandwich
recipes.sub: Sandwich-maker meals
recipes.intro: About 15 g of protein per sandwich.
recipes.parentIntro: The sandwich maker toasts and seals in 3–4 minutes with no flipping. The method is the same for every filling: preheat until the ready light comes on, butter the outsides thinly (¼ tsp a side), don't overfill, toast 3–4 minutes until golden, and let it rest a minute before biting; the filling is very hot.
steps: Spread the chutney inside, add the tikka and onion, close and toast 3–4 minutes.

recipes.title: Omelette pockets (no bread)
recipes.sub: Sandwich-maker meals
recipes.intro: About 12 g of protein.
recipes.parentIntro: The sandwich maker toasts and seals in 3–4 minutes with no flipping. The method is the same for every filling: preheat until the ready light comes on, butter the outsides thinly (¼ tsp a side), don't overfill, toast 3–4 minutes until golden, and let it rest a minute before biting; the filling is very hot.

items.name: 1 tbsp each finely chopped onion, tomato and coriander
A pinch each of chilli, turmeric and salt
¼ tsp oil for the plates

steps: Brush the preheated plates with oil, pour the egg mixture into the lower plates, close gently and cook 4–5 minutes until puffed and set. If your plates leak at the hinge, use less egg.

recipes.title: Bombay veg masala toast
recipes.sub: Sandwich-maker meals
recipes.intro: About 6 g of protein; 13 g with paneer slices.
recipes.parentIntro: The sandwich maker toasts and seals in 3–4 minutes with no flipping. The method is the same for every filling: preheat until the ready light comes on, butter the outsides thinly (¼ tsp a side), don't overfill, toast 3–4 minutes until golden, and let it rest a minute before biting; the filling is very hot.

items.name: 1 small boiled potato, mashed with salt, chilli and chaat masala
Thin slices of cucumber, tomato and onion
40 g paneer slices or a cheese slice (optional)

steps: Spread chutney on both slices, then the potato, then layer the vegetables (and paneer). Close, butter and toast 4 minutes. The Mumbai street classic.

recipes.title: Phulka toastie
recipes.sub: Sandwich-maker meals
recipes.intro: About 10–13 g of protein. Uses a phulka kept from last night.
recipes.parentIntro: The sandwich maker toasts and seals in 3–4 minutes with no flipping. The method is the same for every filling: preheat until the ready light comes on, butter the outsides thinly (¼ tsp a side), don't overfill, toast 3–4 minutes until golden, and let it rest a minute before biting; the filling is very hot.

items.name: 50 g paneer bhurji, or 1 egg made into bhurji

steps: Spread chutney on half the phulka, add the filling and fold it over (fold again into a triangle if your plates are triangular). Brush with ghee and toast 3 minutes until crisp.

recipes.title: Green chutney (mint-coriander)
recipes.sub: Fresh chutneys
recipes.intro: For chillas, sandwiches, rolls and tandoori chicken.
recipes.parentIntro: Each of these is ground in the small mixie jar. Without a fridge, make them on the day: fresh coconut and herb chutneys turn quickly.
steps: Grind everything until smooth, adding the water a little at a time. The lemon keeps it green; the chana gives body so it doesn't separate. Use less water for a sandwich spread.

recipes.title: Coconut chutney
recipes.sub: Fresh chutneys
recipes.intro: For chillas, dosa, idli and ragi rotti.
recipes.parentIntro: Each of these is ground in the small mixie jar. Without a fridge, make them on the day: fresh coconut and herb chutneys turn quickly.

items.name: ½ cup fresh grated coconut (or 3 tbsp desiccated, soaked 10 min in warm water)
Tempering: 1 tsp oil, mustard, urad dal, curry leaves, dried red chilli

steps: Grind the coconut, chana, chillies, ginger and salt with the water until smooth. Heat the oil, crackle the mustard, fry the urad dal golden with the curry leaves and red chilli, and pour over.

recipes.title: Peanut chutney
recipes.sub: Fresh chutneys
recipes.intro: Andhra style; good with chillas and rotti.
recipes.parentIntro: Each of these is ground in the small mixie jar. Without a fridge, make them on the day: fresh coconut and herb chutneys turn quickly.

items.name: Optional tempering as for coconut chutney

steps: No roasted peanuts? Air-fry raw ones at 160 °C for 8–10 minutes, shaking twice. Grind everything to a smooth, thick paste. Temper if you like.

recipes.title: Tomato-onion chutney
recipes.sub: Fresh chutneys
recipes.intro: Cooked, so it keeps through the day.
recipes.parentIntro: Each of these is ground in the small mixie jar. Without a fridge, make them on the day: fresh coconut and herb chutneys turn quickly.
steps: Air-fryer route: toss the onion, halved tomatoes and garlic with ½ tsp oil and air-fry at 200 °C for 10–12 minutes until soft and charred, and fry only the dals and chillies in the pan. On the stove: fry the dals and chillies in the oil until golden, add the onion and garlic for 4 minutes, then the tomatoes, tamarind and salt for 6–8 minutes until soft. Cool and grind. Temper if you like.

recipes.title: Shenga chutney pudi (peanut)
recipes.sub: Chutney powders that keep
recipes.intro: Keeps about 2 weeks (the garlic shortens it).
recipes.parentIntro: Dry-roasted, coarsely ground powders that need no fridge. Peanuts and dals can be roasted in the air fryer (160 °C, 8–10 minutes, shaking every 3), but roast flaxseeds and sesame in a pan: the fan scatters them. A spoonful mixed with a little ghee, oil or curd turns a plain phulka, rotti or chilla into a meal. The first two are North Karnataka classics.
steps: Dry-roast the peanuts on low for 5–6 minutes until the skins crack and they smell toasty; cool and rub off the skins. Roast the chillies for a minute. Pulse everything in short bursts to a coarse powder; long grinding releases the peanut oil and turns it into paste.

recipes.title: Agasi chutney pudi (flaxseed)
recipes.sub: Chutney powders that keep
recipes.intro: Keeps 2–3 weeks.
recipes.parentIntro: Dry-roasted, coarsely ground powders that need no fridge. Peanuts and dals can be roasted in the air fryer (160 °C, 8–10 minutes, shaking every 3), but roast flaxseeds and sesame in a pan: the fan scatters them. A spoonful mixed with a little ghee, oil or curd turns a plain phulka, rotti or chilla into a meal. The first two are North Karnataka classics.
steps: Dry-roast the flaxseeds on low for 3–4 minutes until they pop and smell nutty. Roast the chillies and curry leaves until crisp. Cool, then pulse everything to a coarse powder.

recipes.title: Gunpowder (idli podi)
recipes.sub: Chutney powders that keep
recipes.intro: Keeps about a month.
recipes.parentIntro: Dry-roasted, coarsely ground powders that need no fridge. Peanuts and dals can be roasted in the air fryer (160 °C, 8–10 minutes, shaking every 3), but roast flaxseeds and sesame in a pan: the fan scatters them. A spoonful mixed with a little ghee, oil or curd turns a plain phulka, rotti or chilla into a meal. The first two are North Karnataka classics.
steps: Roast each dal separately on low for 5–6 minutes until golden and aromatic, the chillies for a minute and the sesame until it pops. Cool completely and grind to a slightly coarse powder with the hing and salt. Mix with oil or ghee to eat with chillas, dosa or idli.

recipes.title: Raitas and kachumber
recipes.sub: Cooling sides for every plate
recipes.intro: Made with the curd you set the night before. Make raita just before eating or packing; vegetables release water as it stands.

items.name: Cucumber, grated and squeezed, or finely chopped

steps: Whisk. Whisk the curd with the salt and 1–2 tbsp water until smooth and just pourable.
Mix. Stir in the cucumber and herbs, and sprinkle the cumin and chilli on top.
var: Onion-tomato raita. Use finely chopped onion (soaked 5 minutes in water and drained) and tomato instead of cucumber, with a chopped green chilli.
Boondi raita. Soak 3 tbsp store-bought boondi (it keeps for weeks) in warm water for 2 minutes, squeeze gently and stir in.
Hung-curd mint dip. Hung curd with chopped mint, garlic, salt and pepper: a thick dip for tandoori chicken with about twice the protein.
Kachumber salad. Dice cucumber, tomato and onion into 5 mm pieces. Just before serving, add lemon juice, a pinch each of salt, chilli powder and chaat masala, and chopped coriander.

recipes.title: Andhra-Style Chicken Dum Biryani
recipes.sub: Spicy, layered, sealed on dum
recipes.intro: Andhra biryani is the spicy branch of the dum family. Compared with Hyderabadi biryani it uses more fresh green chilli and red chilli, more mint, and a masala built on browned onion and tomato. The chicken is cooked to 85% in that masala (the pakki method), covered with 75% rice, sealed and finished on dum.

items.name: Bone-in chicken, biryani cut
items.note: Thighs and drumsticks stay juiciest; 70–100 g pieces.

items.name: Spicy red chilli powder (Guntur)
items.note: The Andhra heat. Kashmiri gives colour with less fire.

items.name: Green chillies, for paste
items.note: Crushed with a pinch of salt; half here, half in the masala.

steps: Make the chilli paste and marinate. Crush 3 green chillies with a pinch of salt to a coarse paste. Rinse, drain and dry the chicken and slash the thick pieces (Prep school: Chicken). In a bowl, whisk the curd until smooth. Add the ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, turmeric, biryani masala, salt, lemon juice, half the chilli paste and half the mint, torn. Taste a tiny bit: it should be bold and slightly too salty. Add the chicken and massage the marinade into every piece for a full minute, working it into the cuts. Cover and keep in the coolest, shadiest spot.

Slice, chop and set up. Slice both onions 2–3 mm with the grain and keep them in separate piles. Chop the tomato and coriander. Put the saffron into the warm milk. Knead the sealing dough and roll it into a rope (Prep school). Set out the kadai, slotted spoon, a plate for the birista and the colander.

Fry the birista. Heat the oil in the kadai on medium-high. Add the large onion and fry as in Master technique 1: stir every minute until light gold (about 8 minutes), then lower to medium and stir constantly. Lift it out at deep golden with a reddish tinge and spread it thin on the plate. Strain the oil into a bowl and keep it.
Wash and soak the rice. Wash the basmati gently 3–4 times until the water is only slightly cloudy, then soak it in fresh water (Prep school: Washing and soaking rice). It needs at least 30 minutes.

Cook the chicken masala to 85%. Use the heavy 2 L pot; the dum happens in it later. Heat 2 tbsp birista oil on medium. Temper the bay leaf, cardamom, cloves and cinnamon for 30 seconds until the cloves puff. Add the masala onion and fry 6–7 minutes until golden. Add the tomato and slit chillies and cook 3 minutes until the tomato is soft enough to mash with the spoon. Add the chicken with all its marinade, the rest of the chilli paste and a quarter of the birista, crushed between your fingers. Cook on high for 5 minutes, stirring, so the marinade sets onto the chicken without catching on the bottom. Cover and cook on medium-low for 15 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes. If the gravy is still thin at the end, uncover and cook 2–3 minutes more.
Boil the rice water. Put the water in the large vessel with the salt, the rice-water whole spices, a few mint leaves and 1 tsp oil. Bring it to a rolling boil while the chicken cooks.

Par-boil the rice to 75%. Drain the soaked rice and tip it into the rolling boil. Stir once, gently. Boil uncovered for 5–6 minutes, testing a grain from minute 4 (Master technique 5). At 75%, drain at once in the colander. Don't rinse. If the chicken isn't ready yet, delay putting the rice in rather than leaving drained rice waiting.

Layer and seal. Put the tawa on Burner 1 on medium to preheat. Spread the chicken masala flat in its pot. Spoon the rice on loosely, without pressing. Scatter the remaining birista, mint and the coriander. Drizzle the saffron milk in thin lines and spots, then spoon the ghee over the top. Don't mix. Press the dough rope round the rim, set the lid on and press the dough up against the lid all the way round (Master techniques 6 and 7).

Dum. Keep the pot on high on Burner 2 for 2 minutes until you hear a faint hiss inside. Move it onto the hot tawa on Burner 1 and turn that burner to its lowest steady flame for 18 minutes. Turn the pot a quarter turn every 5 minutes. Don't open it.

Rest and serve. Leave the pot sealed for 10 minutes. Break the seal and check that the top grains are cooked and separate. Slide a flat spatula down the side to the bottom and lift, so every plate gets masala, chicken and all three colours of rice. Serve with onion raita or mirchi ka salan, a lemon wedge and half a boiled egg.

tips.title: Air-fryer route
tips.text: Air-fry the birista instead (Part 4): 1 tbsp oil, 160 °C, 15–25 minutes, tossing every 5 minutes. Burner 1 and your hands stay free, and you use about 70 ml less oil. With no birista oil, cook the masala in step 5 in 2 tbsp fresh oil and stir a pinch of crushed birista into it first.

tips.title: Hotel technique: graded rice
tips.text: Lift the rice with a spider in three batches a minute apart instead of draining it all at once: the least-cooked batch at the bottom, the most-cooked on top.

recipes.title: Lucknowi (Awadhi) Paneer Biryani
recipes.sub: Mild, creamy and perfumed
recipes.intro: Awadhi cooking, from the kitchens of Lucknow's nawabs, prizes fragrance over fire. Its biryani is a pakki biryani with two signatures: the rice is boiled in yakhni (a spiced stock) instead of water, and the gravy is enriched with ground golden onions and cashews. There's no red chilli powder; the warmth comes from white pepper, and the finish from saffron, ghee, kewra and rose water.

items.name: Birista
items.note: Half the batch, ground into the marinade.

items.name: Ghee
items.note: 1 tbsp to sear, 1 tbsp to temper.

steps: Start the yakhni. Yakhni is a spiced stock; here the rice is boiled in it instead of plain water. Tie the yakhni spices and ginger in the muslin to make a potli, or leave them loose to strain later. Put them in the large vessel with the water, bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered on low for 25 minutes.

Soak the cashews, cut the paneer and onion. Soak the cashews in 3 tbsp hot water. Cut the paneer into 1-inch cubes and leave them in warm salted water (Prep school: Paneer). Slice the onion 2–3 mm with the grain.
Wash and soak the rice. Wash the basmati gently 3–4 times and soak it in fresh water. It soaks until step 8.
Fry the birista, one shade lighter. Fry the onion as in Master technique 1, but lift it out at an even golden colour, just before deep golden. Spread it on the plate and keep the oil.

Strain the yakhni and make the marinade. Lift out the potli, squeezing it against the side, or strain out the loose spices. Add the salt, return the yakhni to Burner 3 and keep it on low. In the small mixie jar, grind the drained cashews, half the birista and the curd until completely smooth, scraping down twice. This birista paste gives Awadhi gravy its creamy, golden, gently sweet body. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste, white pepper, cardamom powder, garam masala and salt.

Sear the paneer and let it rest. Heat 1 tbsp ghee in the small heavy pot on medium. Drain the paneer, pat it dry and sear it in one layer, about 1 minute on each of two sides, until it has light golden patches. Tip it into the marinade and fold gently. Leave it for 15 minutes. Meanwhile, put the saffron in the warm milk, roll the sealing dough and pick the mint.

Cook the paneer masala. At 0:43, turn the yakhni on Burner 3 to high so it's boiling for step 8. In the same pot, heat 1 tbsp ghee on medium. Temper the bay leaf, cardamom and shahi jeera for 30 seconds, until the shahi jeera crackles. Add the slit chillies for 10 seconds. Turn the flame to its lowest before adding the paneer with all its marinade. Fold gently for 5 minutes until the gravy thickens and ghee glistens at the edges. Stir in the cream and turn off.
Par-boil the rice in the yakhni. Drain the rice and add it to the boiling yakhni. Stir once. Boil uncovered 5–6 minutes, testing from minute 4. At 75%, drain immediately without rinsing.

Layer and seal. Put the tawa on Burner 1 on medium to preheat. Spread the paneer gravy flat in its pot. Spoon on half the rice, sprinkle half the saffron milk and half the perfumes, then add the rest of the rice. Finish with the remaining saffron milk in streaks, the remaining birista, the ghee, the rest of the rose and kewra water, and the mint. Seal with the dough rope.
Dum. Keep the pot on high for 2 minutes until it hisses, then move it onto the hot tawa on the lowest flame for 12 minutes. Paneer needs less dum than chicken because nothing inside is raw.

Rest and serve. Rest sealed for 10 minutes, then open and lift gently from the sides. Garnish with a few cashews (air-fried at 160 °C for 3–4 minutes) and saffron strands. Serve with burani raita; skip spicy sides so the fragrance stays the star.

tips.title: Air-fryer route
tips.text: Air-fry it instead (Part 4) and take it out at an even golden colour, usually after 12–18 minutes. This recipe never uses the frying oil, so you lose nothing and save about 75 ml of oil.

tips.title: Insurance against splitting
tips.text: Whisk 1 tsp besan or cornflour into the marinade. It stabilises the curd so it stays smooth when heated.

tips.title: Air-fryer route
tips.text: Toss the dried paneer with ½ tsp ghee and air-fry at 200 °C for 5–6 minutes, shaking once, until lightly spotted. It saves most of the searing ghee and leaves Burner 2 free.

recipes.title: Bengaluru Donne-Style Mushroom Biryani
recipes.sub: Green, peppery, one-pot
recipes.intro: Donne biryani is Bengaluru's own. It comes from the city's old "military hotels" (non-vegetarian eateries) and is served in a donne, a cup pressed from dried areca palm leaf. It's different from layered biryani in three ways: the masala is green (mint, coriander, green chilli and whole spices ground raw), the rice is short-grain seeraga samba, and the rice cooks in the masala by absorption rather than being boiled and drained. The mushroom version is a Bengaluru favourite; chicken, mutton and prawn versions are in Part 3.

items.name: Oil
items.note: 1 tbsp for the mushrooms, 2 tbsp for the base.

steps: Wash and soak the rice. Wash the seeraga samba gently 3 times and soak it for 30 minutes. It's small and sturdier than basmati, but still handle it gently.
Clean the mushrooms and slice the vegetables. Clean and quarter the mushrooms (Prep school: Mushrooms) and spread them on a cloth to dry. Slice the onion and chop the tomato.

Grind the green masala. Put the whole spices (cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, fennel, pepper, poppy seeds, stone flower) in the mixie jar and grind dry for 10 seconds. Add the mint, coriander, chillies, ginger and garlic with 3–4 tbsp of the coldest water you have. Grind in short bursts to a smooth paste, like a thick chutney.

Sear the mushrooms dry. Heat 1 tbsp oil in the wide pan on high. Add the mushrooms in one layer and leave them for 2 minutes without stirring. They'll release water; keep cooking on high, tossing now and then, until it has boiled away and the edges are brown, 6–8 minutes in all. Add a pinch of salt only at the end. Set aside. Do step 5 at the same time.

Fry the onion base. Use the heavy 2 L pot; the rice cooks and steams in it. Heat 2 tbsp oil and the ghee on medium. Temper the bay leaf and star anise for 30 seconds. Add the onion and fry about 8 minutes until golden, lighter than birista. At the same time, put the measured water on Burner 3 to heat.

Cook the green masala. Add the tomato and cook 2 minutes until soft. Add all the green paste, the turmeric and ½ tsp of the salt. Cook on medium, stirring, for 6–7 minutes; cover partly if it spatters. Lower the heat, stir in the curd, then add the seared mushrooms and cook 1 minute.

Add the rice and water. Drain the rice completely and add it to the pot. Stir gently for 1 minute so every grain is coated. Pour in the hot water, the rest of the salt and the lemon juice. Boil on high, uncovered, without stirring, for 6–8 minutes, until the water has dropped to the level of the rice and small holes appear across the surface. If one side looks higher, level it once with the back of a spoon.

Dum. Put the tawa on Burner 2 to preheat as soon as the mushroom pan is off (about 0:33). Cover the pot tightly, with foil under the lid or a dough seal, move it onto the hot tawa, and cook on the lowest steady flame for 15 minutes. Don't open the lid.
Rest and serve. Rest covered for 10 minutes, then fluff gently from the sides with a fork. Serve in areca-leaf donnes (they're inexpensive online) with onion raita and a lemon wedge.

tips.title: Air-fryer route
tips.text: Toss the mushrooms with 1 tsp oil and air-fry at 200 °C for 8–10 minutes, shaking twice; salt them afterwards. Burner 2 and your hands are then free for the onion base.

recipes.title: Chicken + Paneer for Five
recipes.sub: Two biryanis from one shared base
recipes.intro: Use this when you're cooking for guests and want both a chicken and a vegetarian biryani on the table at the same time. It uses the techniques from Part 1 and a classic Hyderabadi-style shared base.

items.name: Large onions
items.note: Sliced 2–3 mm; fry in two batches.

steps: Make the shared marinade; marinate the chicken. Whisk all the marinade ingredients. Scoop one-third into a small covered bowl for the paneer. Massage the rest into the cleaned, slashed chicken and leave it in a cool, shady spot.
Prep. Slice the onions, cube and soak the paneer, pick and chop the herbs, and start the saffron soaking.
Fry the birista in two batches. Fry two onions at a time in the oil (Master technique 1). Keep the oil.
Wash and soak the rice. Wash and soak all 500 g of basmati.
Marinate the paneer; make two dough ropes. Fold the drained paneer into its third of the marinade. Knead ½ cup atta and roll two ropes, one for each pot.

Chicken masala to 85%. In the larger heavy pot, heat 3 tbsp birista oil, add the chicken with its marinade and a quarter of the birista, crushed. Cook on high 7 minutes, then cover and cook on medium-low about 18 minutes, stirring every 5, until 85% done with thick, clinging gravy.
Boil the rice water. 3 L water with the salt and whole spices, to a rolling boil.

Paneer masala. In the smaller heavy pot, heat 1 tbsp birista oil, add the paneer with its marinade and a small handful of crushed birista. Cook gently on medium-low for 5–6 minutes until thick. No longer: paneer turns rubbery.
Par-boil all the rice to 75%. Boil 5–7 minutes, testing from minute 4, and drain.

Layer both pots. Preheat the tawa on Burner 1 and a thick steel plate on Burner 3. Put 60% of the rice over the chicken and 40% over the paneer. Split the birista, herbs, saffron milk, ghee and kewra between the two. Seal both.

Dum both pots. Give each pot 2 minutes on high, then move the chicken onto the tawa (Burner 1) and the paneer onto the plate (Burner 3), both on the lowest flame. Paneer: 10 minutes. Chicken: 20 minutes.
Rest and serve. Rest each pot 10 minutes after its dum ends; a sealed pot stays hot for well over 20 minutes, so the paneer waits happily for the chicken. Serve both together.
